channel.title: Kukie Serving on History
channel.description: Recent content in Kukie Serving on History

item.title: Kukie Serving.09 Self-Training Rounds
item.description: How Kukie trained Qwen3.8-27B on its own filtered solutions to Kubernetes faults — why the 9B student route stopped, a first round that broke nothing but proved nothing, three weaknesses picked from an external benchmark, a second round whose collection and training both hit pre-registered stop conditions, and a single frozen measurement that judged it improved on 44 unseen external problems (+6.1%p, CI +0.8 to +12.0) before release as Kause-K8s-27B v0.2.

item.title: Kukie Serving.08 Evaluation Design
item.description: How Kukie measures a small Kubernetes-diagnosis model before training it — a kind harness that plants a fault and checks the symptom before the agent runs, a verdict based only on exact cause category and cause object, evidence v2 kept as a side metric, sets that changed role as baselines exposed shortcuts (a no-LLM baseline scoring 67.7%), four contamination paths with the one we could not block, and a pre-registered decision rule with guards, stop conditions and recorded deviations.

item.title: Kukie Serving.07 API Gateway and Connector
item.description: How one public Kukie API address reaches models on customers’ own GPU clusters — Kotlin keeps accounts, permissions, keys and usage, a Go gateway relays JSON/SSE without storing bodies, and a connector inside each customer cluster dials out over WebSocket; plus the load test that moved key checks off the request path (member CPU 0.67 to 0.02 cores, ITL p95 72.5 to 29.3ms) and a 31-hour outage caused by credential re-issue.

item.title: Kukie Serving.06 Counter and Adaptive Limit
item.description: How kukie-counter, a Go proxy in front of vLLM, sets each model’s concurrency limit — first from the measured baseline × 0.8, then from the TTFT and ITL p95 it times on every stream (+1 / ×0.7 every 5 s) with a waiting-queue brake — and what two load tests on one L40S showed: 16 → 21 under SLA, a cascading cut on long prompts, and a 20 ms stall that lives in the proxy path, not in vLLM.

item.title: Kukie Serving.05 Cold Start Path
item.description: Where the minutes go between a start button and a ready vLLM pod on a fresh GPU node — the engine image pulled into the node’s root EBS on every new node, the weights kept on a separate PVC EBS that outlives the node, and a 65GB read that ran at exactly the gp3 baseline of 125 MiB/s.

item.title: Kukie Serving.03 ServedModel Operator
item.description: Building kukie-oven, a Go operator that turns one ServedModel into a PVC, a download Job and a vLLM Deployment — the reconcile order, two server-side-apply field managers, telling someone else’s object from a leftover, Helm and GHCR packaging, an EBS CSI role limited by a tag boundary, and the first real run on an L40S: Ready in 14 minutes 11 seconds with no manual step.

item.title: Kukie Serving.02 GPU Add-on Design
item.description: Why an external LLM API plan became a Helm add-on for users’ GPU clusters — quality and cost numbers behind the pivot, three layers split by required permissions, a chart with per-layer switches and a preflight job, the measurement-to-429 loop, an honest comparison with KubeAI and LiteLLM, and what is built versus still planned.

item.title: Kukie Serving.01 Baseline on One L40S
item.description: Measuring how many concurrent requests one NVIDIA L40S serves within a latency SLA before building a GPU cluster — the SLA draft as TTFT and inter-token latency, a single g6e.xlarge with two stop guards, a measurement script split from the server so it can run as a Kubernetes Job, results for four open models, why MoE models outrun a dense 27B on memory bandwidth, KV cache FP8 for 20% more headroom, and two review fixes.
